title: Dynamical mass measurements of two protoplanetary discs
question: Measure dynamically the total disc mass of IM Lup and GM Aur from deviations from Keplerianity in $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO rotation curves induced by disc self-gravity and pressure gradients.

what.value: Distances and inclinations of IM Lup (d=158 pc, i=47.5 deg) and GM Aur (d=159 pc, i=53.2 deg)

evidence.quote: Distances and inclinations of the two sources are obtained from the literature. In particular, we adopt the same geometrical parameters as used in MAPS (cite: Oberg21)
| $i$ (degrees) | 47.5$^\circ$ | 53.2$^\circ$ |

what.value: Pressure scale height parameters H0 and q for IM Lup (H0=10 au, q=0.66) and GM Aur (H0=7.5 au, q=0.3)

evidence.quote: we fix the pressure scale height from the thermochemical model of (cite: Zhang21) (which are in very good agreement with the recent analysis of (cite: Paneque22))

what.value: Height of emitting layers of 12CO and 13CO (z0, p, q, Rt) and 2D gas temperature parameterizations for GM Aur

evidence.quote: and the height of the emitting layers of $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO from the MAPS analysis (cite: Law21).

what.value: Dust mass of IM Lup (1.7e-3 M_sun)

evidence.quote: Note that, given the known value of the dust mass of $M_{\rm dust}=1.7~10^{-3}\, \mathrm{M}_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ (cite: Cleeves16), our measurement implies a gas/dust ratio of $\sim 60$, close to the standard assumed value of 100.

what.value: Dust mass of GM Aur (0.002 M_sun)

evidence.quote: The dust mass estimated by (cite: Macias18) is $0.002\, \mathrm{M}_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$, which would translate into $0.2\, \mathrm{M}_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ for the gas mass, assuming a gas/dust ratio of 100.

recipe.goal: Extract rotation curves using EDDY (Simple Harmonic Oscillator method)
recipe.method: Fit line centroids using Gaussian and Quadratic methods and align spectra in annuli with a Simple Harmonic Oscillator (SHO) model deprojected using known disc inclination, position angle, and emitting layer height z(R).
key_parameters: Radial range: from beam FWHM to ~500 au (IM Lup 12CO) and ~400 au (GM Aur both lines and IM Lup 13CO)
Line centroid methods: Gaussian and Quadratic
assumptions: Axisymmetric disc with thin emitting layer z_i(R) and fixed geometry from Table 1

recipe.method: Fit Gaussian or quadratic profiles to line profiles to obtain line-of-sight velocities, model and mask the lower emitting surface, and compute unweighted azimuthal averages of deprojected velocities within [-30, 30] deg around the disc major axis.
key_parameters: Azimuthal averaging window: [-30, 30] deg around major axes
assumptions: Radial and vertical velocity components v_R and v_z are negligible or localised; fixed orientation and emission surfaces from Table 1

recipe.goal: Pre-compute self-gravitating potential contribution on a 2D grid
recipe.method: Numerically integrate the 1D integral for the radial derivative of the disc gravitational potential (Eq. 14) on a 2D grid (R, Z) using QUADPACK and interpolate at (R, z(R)) during MCMC fitting.
assumptions: Tapered power-law surface density profile with gamma = 1

recipe.goal: Fit dynamical model to 12CO and 13CO rotation curves via MCMC
recipe.method: Simultaneously (and for GM Aur also separately) fit 12CO and 13CO rotation curves to the analytical + numerical rotation velocity model including stellar gravity, disc self-gravity, radial pressure gradient, and emitting height z(R) using emcee.
key_parameters: Reference radius R0 = 100 au; fixed parameters from Table 1
assumptions: Vertically isothermal disc in hydrostatic and centrifugal balance; independent data points along the rotation curve; gas-to-dust ratio evaluated against literature dust masses

score_reason: The input spectral cubes are publicly hosted by the MAPS survey, the extraction tools (EDDY and DISCMINER) are public, the authors released their MCMC dynamical fitting code (DySc) on GitHub, and almost all fixed structural parameters, equations, and MCMC settings/priors are explicitly tabulated.
rediscovery_reason: Public MAPS data cubes, public analysis and fitting codes (EDDY, DISCMINER, DySc), well-defined analytical/numerical equations, and clear numeric target quantities (stellar mass, disc mass, scale radius).
